Kuvitus: aurinkoinen järvi, jonka pinnas: Illustration: a sunny lake with bright glare sparkling on its surface. A wooded shore is in the background. In the middle of the picture are sunglasses. Seen through the lenses the glare is gone: the water looks darker and transparent, and the stones and a fish on the bottom are visible.
Periaatekuva vinosti sivulta, ei mittaka: Schematic picture seen obliquely from the side, not to scale: on the left is a lamp that sends unpolarised light to the right. The electric field of the light oscillates perpendicular to the direction of travel in many different directions, shown by brown double arrows in different positions. The light passes through a polarising film, whose hatching and dark line show a vertical transmission axis. After the film the electric field oscillates only in the vertical direction, shown by a brown wave in a vertical plane, and the intensity is half of the original. At the bottom small circles show the directions of oscillation seen along the ray: many directions before the film, only the vertical direction after it.
Periaatekuva: kaksi paria pyöreitä polar: Schematic picture: two pairs of round polarising films on a light table. The hatching of the films shows the transmission axis. On the left the transmission axes of the films are the same, the angle is 0 degrees, and the overlapping part is only a little darker than a single film. On the right the transmission axis of one film is vertical and that of the other horizontal, the angle is 90 degrees, and the overlapping part is almost black.
Periaatekuva sivulta, ei mittakaavassa:: Schematic picture from the side, not to scale: sunlight arrives from the upper left at the surface of a lake. The incoming ray has both dots, which mean oscillation perpendicular to the plane of the paper, that is, parallel to the water surface, and double arrows in the plane of the paper: the light is unpolarised. The ray reflected from the surface has mostly dots: the glare is partially polarised in the horizontal direction. On the right the reflected light meets polarised sunglasses whose transmission axis is vertical, so only a weak ray continues to the eye after the glasses. Part of the light is refracted into the water.
Kaavakuva säteen suunnasta katsottuna: p: Diagram seen along the ray: the amplitude E0 of the electric field of polarised light points vertically upwards, so the light is polarised in the vertical direction. The transmission axis of the analyser is at an angle theta from the vertical. The component E0 cos theta of the electric field along the transmission axis passes through, and the perpendicular component E0 sin theta is absorbed. In the picture the angle theta is 35 degrees.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: polarisoituneen v: Graph to scale: the share I over I0 of the intensity of polarised light that passes through a polariser, as a function of the angle theta from zero to 180 degrees. The curve cos squared theta starts at the value 1, first falls gently, is 0.50 at 45 degrees and zero at 90 degrees, and then rises symmetrically back to 1 at 180 degrees. Marked points: 30 degrees 0.75; 45 degrees 0.50; 60 degrees 0.25.
Kaavakuva, kulmat mittakaavassa: valo tu: Diagram with the angles to scale: light arrives from air at the water surface at Brewster's angle alpha B = 53.1 degrees from the normal. The incoming ray has both dots, meaning oscillation perpendicular to the plane of the paper, and double arrows in the plane of the paper. The reflected ray leaves at the same angle and is completely polarised: it has only dots, so the electric field oscillates parallel to the water surface. The refracted ray continues into the water at an angle alpha 2 = 36.9 degrees and has mostly double arrows. There is a right angle between the reflected and the refracted ray.
Kuvitus: pöydällä on puhelin, jonka näyt: Illustration: on a table is a phone with a bright display. A square grey polarising film has been placed obliquely on the display. The part of the display under the film looks almost black, and the corner of the film that is outside the display looks only slightly grey.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: puhelimen näytön: Graph to scale: light from a phone display through a polarising film. On the horizontal axis is cos squared theta, where theta is the angle of rotation of the film, from zero to one, grid spacing 0.1. On the vertical axis is the reading E of a light sensor in lux from zero to 400, grid spacing 25 lux. Seven data points at the angles 0, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 90 degrees: 374, 354, 283, 197, 102, 40 and 15 lux. A straight line has been fitted to the points; it rises steadily from the left edge, where it is at about 15 lux, to the right edge, where it is at about 375 lux.
